advances: The complete affine-height tree family has A(w) >= W^2/(40*2^N), uniformly as its entrance counts and dimensions are rebuilt. Thus this many-level family does not refute the proposed integrated averaging inequality. The proof applies the inverse-path staircase at every tree level, retains the entire final entrance block, and sums positive contributions from one explicitly chosen height in every tree column. It requires the inverse-chain partition together with a cube at every prefix. No existence of these structures, or integrated lower bound, is asserted for general tables.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The complete affine-height support, rebuilt parameters, global extension, and exact census are consumed from `604889294a17d7df`; the logarithmic hitting conventions and closed-cap characterization from `488f0a583886b5fc`; and the inverse-chain partition from `c2b7164e5a46e1b3`. The cube extension at arbitrary prefixes, all local cap estimates, the final-height case, and the weighted summation are proved analytically above. No computational certificate or numerical feasibility claim is used.
proof:
The accepted exact support and global log-concave extension in `604889294a17d7df` apply to this table, including its zeros. For every positive barycentric representation at \(\mathbf J=(j,h)\), the height identity is \(\sum_{\mathbf I=(z,t)\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf I}t=h\). Consequently its logarithmic gap is exactly \((\sum\lambda_{\mathbf I}t-h)\log2=0\). The support reduction in `488f0a583886b5fc` identifies hitting all these supports with its affinely independent support convention. This proves the first identity in (2). The second follows from \(\int_0^\infty e^{-L}\,dL=1\) and the finiteness of \(D\).

We first identify the hitting minimum with ordinary weighted halfspace depth on the full lifted table. At cutoff zero, the exact logarithmic cap formula of `488f0a583886b5fc` gives scores

\[
\mathbf b\cdot(z-j)+c(t-h)
+\tau\bigl(\phi_{\mathbf J}-\phi_{(z,t)}\bigr)
=\mathbf b\cdot(z-j)+(c-\tau\log2)(t-h),
\qquad \tau\ge0.
\]

Here \(\tau\) is that fact's last normal coefficient, while \(t\) remains the actual integer height. Every nonzero effective normal in \(\mathbb R^N\) is available by taking \(\tau=0\). A zero effective normal includes all of \(D\), of weight \(W\), and therefore cannot lower the minimum over the nonzero effective normals. It follows that

\[
m((j,h))=
\min_{(\mathbf b,c)\ne(\mathbf0,0)}
\sum_{\substack{(z,t)\in D\\
\mathbf b\cdot(z-j)+c(t-h)\ge0}}2^{-t}.
\tag{3}
\]

These are closed halfspaces. Equality atoms are retained throughout the proof.

We recall the exact inverse-chain partition proved in `c2b7164e5a46e1b3`. For every Boolean vector \(j\in\{0,1\}^n\), invert \(F_{m_{\mathrm{br}}}\) on the successive visited child blocks of \(j\), stopping when an inverse does not exist. This gives distinct coordinates \(u_1,\ldots,u_{h_-(j)}\), each having \(j_{u_i}=1\). Define \(z^+_{j,s}=j+\sum_{i=1}^s\mathbf e_{u_i}\). Then

\[
A_{m_{\mathrm{br}},Q}
=\bigsqcup_{j\in\{0,1\}^n}
\{z^+_{j,s}:0\le s\le h_-(j)\},
\qquad \operatorname{lev}(z^+_{j,s})=s.
\tag{4}
\]

This is exactly that accepted partition, with its \(n_{\mathrm{tree}}\) equal to our \(n\). In particular no tree point is counted twice. The root \(j\) associated with a tree point is obtained by replacing every two by one.

We need the cube property at every prefix of (4), so we verify it directly. Fix \(j\), put \(h_-=h_-(j)\), and fix \(0\le s\le h_-\). Write \(z=z^+_{j,s}\), \(q=h_--s\), and \(\mathbf v_i=\mathbf e_{u_{s+i}}\) for \(1\le i\le q\). Then all points

\[
z-\sum_{i\in B}\mathbf v_i\quad(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\})
\quad\text{belong to level }s,
\qquad
z+\sum_{i=1}^r\mathbf v_i=z^+_{j,s+r}
\quad(1\le r\le q)
\tag{5}
\]

belong to the exact tree support. The second assertion is part of (4). For the first, replace the first \(s\) twos of the displayed cube point by zeros. The resulting Boolean source is
\(\beta_B=j-\sum_{i=1}^s\mathbf e_{u_i}-\sum_{i\in B}\mathbf e_{u_{s+i}}\).
At each of the first \(s\) visited child blocks, its entries are the predecessor under \(F_{m_{\mathrm{br}}}\) of the corresponding block of \(j\). Indeed, the change \(j_{u_i}=1\) to zero produces that predecessor. All other changes used here occur in different child blocks: coordinates at different depths along the path belong to different visited child blocks. In particular the changes with indices greater than \(s\) affect none of the first \(s\) blocks. The forward path of \(\beta_B\) therefore follows \(u_1,\ldots,u_s\). Replacing those selected zeros by twos gives exactly the cube point in (5), proving its membership and level. When \(s=0\), this argument just says that each cube point is Boolean.

The vectors \(\mathbf v_i\) are distinct standard coordinate vectors, hence linearly independent. Thus the \(2^q\) cube points in (5) are distinct. They are also disjoint from every positive staircase prefix in (5), since the latter have strictly larger tree level. Their lifted columns have precisely the respective entrance heights specified in the statement.

We will use one elementary counting inequality. For real numbers \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_q\) and \(u\ge0\), let \(p\) be the number of subsets \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,q\}\) with \(\sum_{i\in B}\alpha_i\le u\). Then \(p\ge1\), and

\[
\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i>(r-p+1)u
\quad\text{whenever }p+1\le r\le q.
\tag{6}
\]

To prove this, among the first \(r\) coordinates take the subset of negative \(\alpha_i\), and write its sum as \(-v\), with \(v\ge0\). This subset is counted. Its \(r\) distinct one-coordinate neighbors have sums \(-v+|\alpha_i|\). At most \(p-1\) of these neighbors are counted. Hence at least \(r-p+1\ge2\) satisfy \(|\alpha_i|>v+u\). Therefore

\[
\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i
=\sum_{i=1}^r|\alpha_i|-2v
>(r-p+1)(v+u)-2v
\ge(r-p+1)u.
\]

All these subsets are subsets of the full \(q\)-coordinate cube, so the count \(p\) indeed bounds them. This proves (6), including \(u=0\). If no index satisfies the displayed range, the assertion is vacuous.

Define the complete column weights \(V_s=\sum_{t=a_s}^k2^{-t}\), for \(0\le s\le Q\). We now prove the following bound for each prefix of each inverse chain. With \(j,s,z,q\) as in (5), select the integer target
\(\mathbf J_{j,s}=(z,\min\{a_s+1,k\})\). This target lies in \(D\). We claim

\[
w_{\mathbf J_{j,s}}\ge\frac{V_s}{4},
\qquad
m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\ge
\frac1{10}\sum_{r=s}^{h_-(j)}V_r.
\tag{7}
\]

First suppose \(a=a_s<k\), and put \(\omega=2^{-a}\). The cube in (5) is present at heights \(a\) and \(a+1\), with weights \(\omega\) and \(\omega/2\). The selected target has height \(a+1\). Retain from staircase prefix \(r\), for \(1\le r\le q\), all its heights \(t\ge\max\{a_{s+r},a+1\}\), through height \(k\). Their total normalized weight is

\[
U=\omega^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^q
\sum_{t=\max\{a_{s+r},a+1\}}^k2^{-t}.
\tag{8}
\]

Every retained height has the form \(t=a+\ell\), with \(\ell\ge1\), and its normalized weight is \(2^{-\ell}\).

Fix an arbitrary halfspace in (3) through this selected target. Let \(V_{\mathrm{cap}}\) be the weight of its intersection with the full support divided by \(\omega\), and let \(U_{\mathrm{in}}\) be the normalized weight of its included retained staircase points. Put \(\alpha_i=\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf v_i\). A retained point at staircase prefix \(r\) and relative height \(\ell\) has score
\(\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i+c(\ell-1)\).

If \(c\ge0\), the cube at height \(a+1\) has exactly \(p\) included vertices, where \(p\) is the number of subsets with \(\sum_{i\in B}\alpha_i\le0\). The empty subset is counted, so \(p\ge1\), and disjointness of cube and staircase gives \(V_{\mathrm{cap}}\ge p/2+U_{\mathrm{in}}\). By (6) with \(u=0\), every prefix \(r>p\) has strictly positive prefix sum. Every retained point at such a prefix is included, since \(\ell\ge1\). Each of the first at most \(p\) prefixes has normalized retained weight at most \(\sum_{\ell\ge1}2^{-\ell}=1\). It follows that

\[
U\le U_{\mathrm{in}}+p
\le2\bigl(U_{\mathrm{in}}+p/2\bigr)
\le2V_{\mathrm{cap}}.
\tag{9}
\]

If \(c<0\), put \(\delta=-c>0\) and use the cube at height \(a\). It has exactly \(p\) included vertices with \(\sum_{i\in B}\alpha_i\le\delta\). Thus \(p\ge1\) and \(V_{\mathrm{cap}}\ge p+U_{\mathrm{in}}\). For prefix \(r=p+v\le q\), with \(v\ge1\), (6) yields \(\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i>(v+1)\delta\). Every retained point at that prefix with \(\ell\le v+2\) consequently has strictly positive score and is included. The total excluded normalized weight at that prefix is at most
\(\sum_{\ell=v+3}^\infty2^{-\ell}=2^{-(v+2)}\).
The first at most \(p\) prefixes again weigh at most \(p\). Summing the remaining geometric majorants gives

\[
U\le U_{\mathrm{in}}+p+\sum_{v=1}^\infty2^{-(v+2)}
=U_{\mathrm{in}}+p+\frac14
\le\frac54V_{\mathrm{cap}}
\le2V_{\mathrm{cap}}.
\tag{10}
\]

For the penultimate inequality, use \(V_{\mathrm{cap}}\ge U_{\mathrm{in}}+p\ge1\). The infinite sums in (9) and (10) only bound finite sums of supported points; no new table atoms are introduced. Both arguments also cover \(q=0\), and cover normals whose restriction to all selected directions vanishes. The halfspace was arbitrary, so (3), (9), and (10) imply \(m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\ge\omega U/2\).

Write \(R=\sum_{r=s+1}^{h_-(j)}V_r\) for the full remaining column weight beyond this prefix. The entrances are nondecreasing. If a descendant has entrance greater than \(a\), none of its heights were removed in (8). If it has entrance equal to \(a\), its full column weight is \(\omega(2-2^{-(k-a)})\), and its retained weight is \(\omega(1-2^{-(k-a)})\). Because \(k-a\ge1\), the retained weight is at least one third of the full weight. Thus \(\omega U\ge R/3\), and \(m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\ge R/6\).

The central singleton also forces \(m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\ge w_{\mathbf J_{j,s}}=\omega/2\). Since \(V_s\le2\omega\), we have \(V_s\le4m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\). Combining these two bounds gives
\(V_s+R\le10m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\).
Finally, \(w_{\mathbf J_{j,s}}=\omega/2\ge V_s/4\). This proves both assertions in (7) when \(a_s<k\).

Now suppose \(a_s=k\), and put \(\omega=2^{-k}\). Every descendant in this chain also has entrance \(k\). The cube and all \(q\) staircase points in (5) are therefore present at the common height \(k\), each with weight \(\omega\). The target is \((z,k)\). For an arbitrary normal in (3), the height term is zero on these selected points. Let \(p\ge1\) be the number of included cube vertices and let \(v\ge0\) be the number of included staircase points. Formula (6) at threshold zero includes every staircase prefix beyond \(p\). Hence \(q\le p+v\). By disjointness, the full cap weight is at least \(\omega(p+v)\), and

\[
\omega(q+1)\le\omega(p+v+1)
\le2\omega(p+v).
\]

Consequently \(m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\ge\omega(q+1)/2\). Here \(\sum_{r=s}^{h_-(j)}V_r=\omega(q+1)\), and \(w_{\mathbf J_{j,s}}=V_s=\omega\), so (7) follows with room to spare. This treats the entire final entrance block, including the terminal prefix with \(q=0\), without discarding any of its columns.

It remains to sum the local bounds against the original weights. The selected targets \(\mathbf J_{j,s}\) are all distinct: their tree coordinates run exactly once over (4). Every other integer target of positive weight contributes a nonnegative term to \(A(w)\). Therefore this selection is a lower bound on the full sum, with all unselected height contributions retained as a nonnegative remainder. From (7),

\[
\begin{aligned}
A(w)
&\ge\sum_{j\in\{0,1\}^n}\sum_{s=0}^{h_-(j)}
w_{\mathbf J_{j,s}}m(\mathbf J_{j,s})\\
&\ge\frac1{40}\sum_{j\in\{0,1\}^n}
\sum_{0\le s\le r\le h_-(j)}V_sV_r\\
&\ge\frac1{80}\sum_{j\in\{0,1\}^n}
\left(\sum_{s=0}^{h_-(j)}V_s\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]

The last inequality follows by expanding the square: the sum over \(s\le r\) is one half of that square plus one half of \(\sum_sV_s^2\). Supplying every tree point in the disjoint partition (4) with its complete height column gives the exact mass identity

\[
\sum_{j\in\{0,1\}^n}\sum_{s=0}^{h_-(j)}V_s=W.
\tag{12}
\]

Thus Cauchy–Schwarz on the exactly \(2^n\) Boolean roots yields

\[
\sum_{j\in\{0,1\}^n}
\left(\sum_{s=0}^{h_-(j)}V_s\right)^2
\ge\frac{W^2}{2^n}.
\tag{13}
\]

Equations (11) and (13) give \(A(w)\ge W^2/(80\cdot2^n)=W^2/(40\cdot2^N)\), proving (1).

For comparison with the complete level census in `604889294a17d7df`, that census and (12) also give \(W=2^n\sum_{s=0}^Q\eta^sV_s\), with \(\eta=1-2^{-m_{\mathrm{br}}}\binom{m_{\mathrm{br}}}{m_{\mathrm{br}}/2}\). No level factor has been omitted or replaced by one in the argument: (12) sums the exact inverse-chain lengths, and hence includes these exact census factors automatically. The proof does not select only the all-ones Boolean root. It selects a valid center in every tree column, including every positive tree level, and uses its remaining inverse-chain mass.

The properties responsible for the bound are the partition of all tree points into these inverse chains, a cube at each prefix with the same entrance as that prefix, the higher prefixes as a staircase in the corresponding independent directions, and two successive height slices whose geometric weights control each column. A general-table extension of this argument would need a decomposition with comparable control of the weight assigned to the local centers and of the remaining source mass. Neither such a decomposition nor a universal integrated lower bound follows from the present family calculation.
statement:
Fix an integer \(k\ge8\), and use exactly the \(\rho_t=2^{-t}\) specialization of accepted fact `604889294a17d7df`, with all parameters rebuilt at this \(k\). Explicitly, set \(b_\ell=0\) for \(1\le\ell<8\), \(b_\ell=\lfloor2^\ell/(8\ell)\rfloor\) for \(8\le\ell\le k\), \(Q_0=0\), \(Q_\ell=\sum_{r=1}^\ell b_r\), and \(Q=Q_k\). Put \(a_0=0\), and put \(a_s=\ell\) when \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\). In particular \(0=a_0\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_Q=k\).

Write \(m_{\mathrm{br}}=2(Q+1)^4\) for the branching parameter called \(m\) in that accepted fact, reserving \(m(\mathbf J)\) for a hitting minimum below. Set \(n=\sum_{r=1}^Q m_{\mathrm{br}}^r\) and \(N=n+1\). The tree coordinates are the words in \(\bigcup_{r=1}^Q[m_{\mathrm{br}}]^r\). Use the same symmetric saturated-chain partition of \(\{0,1\}^{m_{\mathrm{br}}}\) and its partial injective successor \(F_{m_{\mathrm{br}}}\) as in the accepted construction. Given a Boolean tree vector \(\beta\), start at the root and apply this successor to each visited child block. Its changed zero coordinate selects the next child. Stop when the successor is undefined or depth \(Q\) is reached, obtaining the path \(u_1,\ldots,u_{h(\beta)}\). The exact tree support is

\[
A_{m_{\mathrm{br}},Q}
=\left\{\beta+2\sum_{i=1}^s\mathbf e_{u_i}:
\beta\in\{0,1\}^n,\quad 0\le s\le h(\beta)\right\}.
\]

Its level \(\operatorname{lev}(z)\) is the number of coordinates equal to two. Use the full lifted support, including its upper and lower height boundaries,

\[
\begin{aligned}
D&=\{(z,t):z\in A_{m_{\mathrm{br}},Q},\quad
a_{\operatorname{lev}(z)}\le t\le k,\quad t\in\mathbb Z\},\\
w_{(z,t)}&=2^{-t}\quad((z,t)\in D),
\qquad w_{\mathbf I}=0\quad(\mathbf I\in\mathbb Z^N\setminus D),\\
W&=\sum_{\mathbf I\in D}w_{\mathbf I},
\qquad T=\frac{W}{2^N}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For each \(\mathbf J\in D\), a positive barycentric support means a nonempty set \(E\subseteq D\) for which there exist coefficients \(\lambda_{\mathbf I}>0\), summing to one, with \(\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}\lambda_{\mathbf I}\mathbf I=\mathbf J\). Define \(m(\mathbf J)\) to be the minimum of \(\sum_{\mathbf I\in F}w_{\mathbf I}\) over sets \(F\subseteq D\) meeting every such support. Each included source is charged its full original weight, independently of any barycentric coefficient. The singleton \(\{\mathbf J\}\) is among the supports that must be met. Put \(A(w)=\sum_{\mathbf J\in D}w_{\mathbf J}m(\mathbf J)\).

For every integer \(k\ge8\),

\[
A(w)\ge\frac1{40}\frac{W^2}{2^N}=\frac1{40}WT.
\tag{1}
\]

Use the logarithmic hitting conventions of accepted fact `488f0a583886b5fc`, with its integer dimension replaced by \(N\). Its normalized potential is \(\phi_{(z,t)}=t\log2\), because \(w_{\max}=1\). This scalar potential is distinct from the lower entrance-height envelope called \(\phi(x)\) in `604889294a17d7df`. Every positive barycentric support has logarithmic cost zero. Thus, for all \(\mathbf J\in D\) and all \(L\ge0\),

\[
m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)=m(\mathbf J),
\qquad
\sum_{\mathbf J\in D}w_{\mathbf J}
\int_0^\infty e^{-L}m_{\log}(\mathbf J,L;w)\,dL=A(w).
\tag{2}
\]

In particular the ratio in (1) cannot tend to zero on the prescribed family, even though `604889294a17d7df` gives \(T\sim H_k/8\to\infty\), where \(H_k=\sum_{\ell=1}^k1/\ell\).
